External datasets we've used in lab projects over the last few years. Each
page says what's in the dataset, how to get access, and what to watch out for
when you analyze it or publish with it.

## Datasets

::: {#database-pages}
:::

## Access at a glance

| Database | What it is | Access |
|---|---|---|
| [ADNI](adni.qmd) | Longitudinal Alzheimer's cohort: imaging, biomarkers, genetics, cognition | Controlled. Tomás adds lab members |
| [ROSMAP](rosmap.qmd) | Two aging cohorts with brain donation: clinical, neuropathology, omics | Controlled, through Synapse. Tomás adds lab members |
| [SEA-AD](sea-ad.qmd) | Single-cell and spatial atlas of Alzheimer's brain tissue | Open (raw sequencing reads are controlled) |
| [NHANES](nhanes.qmd) | US national health and nutrition survey | Open. Ask Tomás about easier ways to download it |

## Controlled-access data

ADNI and ROSMAP are controlled access: you can only use the data under a data
use agreement. Tomás has access to both and can add students and researchers.
**If you need one of them and Tomás hasn't added you yet, contact Tomás.**

The agreements cover named people, so getting files from a labmate who has
access doesn't count; you need to be added yourself. While you work with the
data:

- Keep it only on systems the agreement allows, and share files only with
  people who have been added.
- Never commit it to a Git repository.
- Don't put it into AI tools, including the lab's Claude organization. See
  [AI Tools and Lab Data](../data/ai-tools-and-lab-data.qmd).
- Follow the dataset's publication rules, listed on its page.

## Adding a database

- One page per dataset: what's in it, how to get access, and anything that
  tripped you up.
- Add a row to the table above.
- No credentials, tokens, or account details on any page. This repo is public.
